questions.questionText: hour 15 minutes You must answer on the multiple choice answer sheet. You will need: Multiple choice answer sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) INSTRUCTIONS • There are forty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. • For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the multiple choice answer sheet. • Follow the instructions on the multiple choice answer sheet. • Write in soft pencil. • Write your name, centre number and candidate number on the multiple choice answer sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. • Do not use correction fluid. • Do not write on any bar codes. • You may use a calculator. INFORMATION • The total mark for this paper is 40. • Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. • Any rough working should be done on this question paper. The frequency f of vibration of a mass m supported by a spring with spring constant k is given by the equation f = Cmpkq where C is a constant with no units. What are the values of p and q? p q
A cathode-ray oscilloscope displays a square wave, as shown. The time-base setting is 0.20ms per division. What is the frequency of the square wave?

options.A: 0.83Hz B 830Hz C 1300Hz D 1700Hz

questions.questionText: A measurement is taken correctly but with a ruler at a significantly higher temperature than that at which the ruler was calibrated. The higher temperature causes the ruler to expand. What describes the effect on the measurement caused by the higher temperature and how the measurement may be improved?

options.A: The measurement will be subject to a random error. The measurement can be made more accurate by taking the average of several repeated measurements.
options.B: The measurement will be subject to a random error. The measurement can be made more precise by taking the average of several repeated measurements.
options.C: The measurement will be subject to a systematic error. The measurement can be made more accurate by taking the average of several repeated measurements.
options.D: The measurement will be subject to a systematic error. The measurement can be made more precise by taking the average of several repeated measurements.

questions.questionText: The velocity of an electric car changes as shown. velocity /kmh–1 0 1 2 3 4 time/s What is the acceleration of the car?

A projectile is fired from point P with velocity V at an angle θ to the horizontal. It lands at point Q, a horizontal distance R from P, after time T. path of projectile V P θ Q horizontal R The acceleration of free fall is g. Air resistance is negligible. Which equation is correct?

options.A: R = VTcosθ

questions.questionText: A car accelerates from rest in a straight line with constant acceleration. Which graph best represents the variation of the momentum p of the car with the distance s travelled by the car?

options.A: B C D p p p p 0 0 0 0 s s s s 0 0 0 0

questions.questionText: The resultant force F on a raindrop of mass m falling with velocity v is given by the equation F = mg – kv2 where k is a constant and g is the acceleration of free fall. What is the velocity of the raindrop when it reaches a constant (terminal) velocity? k k mg mg

options.A: B C D mg mg k k

questions.questionText: A stationary toy gun fires a bullet. Which statement about the bullet and the gun, immediately after firing, is not correct?

options.A: The force exerted on the bullet by the gun has the same magnitude as the force exerted on the gun by the bullet.
options.B: The force exerted on the bullet by the gun is in the opposite direction to the force exerted on the gun by the bullet.
options.C: The gun and the bullet have the same magnitude of momentum.
options.D: The kinetic energy of the gun must equal the kinetic energy of the bullet.

questions.questionText: A wooden block rests on the rough surface of a board. One end of the board is then raised until the block slides down the board at constant velocity v. block v board What describes the forces acting on the block when it is sliding with constant velocity? frictional force on block resultant force on block

options.A: down the board down the board
options.C: up the board down the board

questions.questionText: Which statement best describes a couple?

options.A: a pair of forces of equal magnitude acting in opposite directions which produce rotational motion but not translational motion
options.B: a pair of forces of equal magnitude acting in opposite directions which produce translational motion but not rotational motion
options.C: a pair of forces of equal magnitude acting in the same direction which produce rotational motion but not translational motion
options.D: a pair of forces of equal magnitude acting in the same direction which produce translational motion but not rotational motion

questions.questionText: A uniform rod XY of weight 10.0N is freely hinged to a wall at X. It is held horizontal by a force F acting from Y at an angle of 30° to the horizontal, as shown. F wall 60° 30° X Y 10.0 N What is the value of F?

Four combinations of vectors are shown, each representing all the forces acting on an object. The forces all act in the same plane. The object is in equilibrium. Which combination of vectors could represent the forces acting on the object?

options.A: B

questions.questionText: A rectangular metal bar exerts a pressure of 15200Pa on the horizontal surface on which it rests. The height of the metal bar is 80cm. What is the density of the metal?

A mass attached to the lower end of a spring bounces up and down. At which points in the path of the mass do the gravitational potential energy of the mass (GPE), the elastic potential energy in the spring (EPE) and the kinetic energy of the mass (KE) have their highest values? GPE EPE KE

options.A: bottom middle top

questions.questionText: A block of weight 80N is pushed a distance of 60cm up a slope inclined at 30° to the horizontal. There is a frictional force of 25N between the block and the surface of the slope. 60 cm 80 N 30° weight horizontal What is the work W done against the gravitational force and the work W done against the g f frictional force? W /J W /J g f
A ball is dropped from rest and falls towards the ground. Air resistance is negligible. Which graph shows the variation with speed of the height of the ball above the ground?

options.A: B height height above above ground ground 0 0 0 speed 0 speed
options.C: D height height above above ground ground 0 0 0 speed 0 speed

questions.questionText: Power is transferred through a machine as shown. power input P power output P I O machine power loss P L What is the efficiency of the machine? P P P P

options.A: I B L C L D O P O +P L P I P O P I

questions.questionText: A tensile force is used to extend a sample of a material. The force is then removed. The variation with strain of the applied stress is shown on the graph. Which point on the graph could represent the elastic limit for the material? C B stress A D 0 strain
A tensile force is applied to an unstretched rubber band, causing it to stretch. The tensile force is then removed. Which statement about the rubber band must be correct?

options.A: If the rubber band stretches elastically and plastically, all the work done by the force is converted to thermal energy in the rubber.
options.B: If the rubber band stretches elastically, it obeys Hooke’s law.
options.C: If the rubber band stretches elastically, the gradient of the force–extension graph represents the work done by the force.
options.D: If the rubber band stretches plastically, the rubber band will be longer after the force is removed than it was before the force is applied.

questions.questionText: A sound wave reduces in intensity but maintains a constant frequency as it travels through air. Which statement is correct?

options.A: The maximum displacement of the particles changes between one particle and the next particle.
options.B: The phase difference between adjacent particles is zero.
options.C: The wavelength is the distance between two particles that have a phase difference of 180°.
options.D: Two particles that have a phase difference of 360° have the same maximum displacement.

questions.questionText: The graph shows the variation with time of the displacement of an electromagnetic wave at a point. 3.0 displacement arbitrary units 0 5 10 15 20 25 30 35 40 45 50 55 time / µs –3.0 The wave is travelling in a vacuum. What is the amplitude and what is the wavelength of the wave? amplitude wavelength /arbitrary units /m
A long glass tube is almost completely immersed in a large tank of water. A tuning fork is struck and held just above the open end of the tube as it is slowly raised.

options.A: 220Hz B 440Hz C 660Hz D 880Hz

questions.questionText: A source emitting sound of a single frequency f travels at constant speed directly towards an s observer. The source then passes the observer and continues to move directly away from the observer. The velocity of the source remains constant. Which graph represents the variation with time of the frequency f of the sound heard by the o observer?

options.A: B f f o o f f s s time time
options.C: D f f o o f f s s time time

questions.questionText: What are the names of the electromagnetic waves that have wavelengths in a vacuum of 100pm and of 100µm? wavelength wavelength 100pm 100µm

options.A: γ-rays infrared

questions.questionText: The diagram shows a string stretched between fixed points X and Y. There is a stationary wave on the string. S Q R X Y P T The solid curve shows the string at a position of maximum displacement. The dashed curve shows the other position of maximum displacement. The straight central dashed line shows the mean position of the string. Point S on the string is directly above point P. Point T on the string is directly below Q. Which statement is correct?

options.A: A short time later, point R on the string will be displaced.
options.B: Points S and T on the string move in opposite directions.
options.C: The distance between P and Q is one wavelength.
options.D: Two points on the string that are equal distances from point R vibrate in phase.

questions.questionText: Which statement must be true for diffraction to occur when a wave passes through a gap?

options.A: The wave is able to travel in a vacuum.
options.C: The wave has a large amplitude.
options.D: The wave has a long wavelength.

questions.questionText: Light of a single wavelength is incident normally on two slits that are 0.20mm apart. Interference fringes are observed on a screen that is 5.4m away from the slits. The distance between successive bright fringes is 12mm. What is the wavelength of the light?

options.A: 440nm B 540nm C 650nm D 900nm

questions.questionText: A diffraction grating and a screen are used to determine the single wavelength λ of the light from a source. What is an essential feature of this experiment?

options.A: A curved screen must be used.
options.B: The diffraction angle θ must be measured for at least two interference maxima.
options.C: The light waves incident on the grating must be coherent.
options.D: The third order intensity maximum must be produced.

questions.questionText: A small charge q is placed in the electric field of a large charge Q. Both charges experience a force F. What is the electric field strength of the charge Q at the position of the charge q? F F F

options.A: B C FqQ D Qq Q q

The particle has a mass of 3.34 × 10–27kg. What is the charge on the particle?
The current in the circuit shown is 3.2mA. R X Y What are the direction of flow and the rate of flow of electrons through the resistor R? direction of flow rate of flow/s–1
Which graph best represents the way the current I through a filament lamp varies with the potential difference V across it?

options.A: B C D I I I I 0 0 0 0 0 V 0 V 0 V 0 V

questions.questionText: A cylindrical metal wire X has resistance R. The same volume of the same metal is made into a cylindrical wire Y of double the length. What is the resistance of wire Y?

options.A: R B 2R C 4R D 8R

questions.questionText: A cell of electromotive force (e.m.f.) E and internal resistance r is connected to a resistor of resistance R.

options.A: R B R C (R−r) D (R+r) (R−r) (R+r) R R

questions.questionText: Three identical resistors can be connected together in four different ways. The resistances of two of these combinations are 4.0Ω and 9.0Ω. What is the resistance of each individual resistor?

options.A: 3.0Ω B 6.0Ω C 12Ω D 18Ω

questions.questionText: In the circuit shown, a battery of negligible internal resistance is connected in series with a pair of fixed resistors R and R .
An element has two isotopic forms. What are the nuclear arrangements of these two isotopes?

options.A: They have different nucleon numbers and different proton numbers.
options.B: They have different nucleon numbers but the same proton number.
options.C: They have the same nucleon number and the same proton number.
options.D: They have the same nucleon number but different proton numbers.
